ai.description: *Ombrana sikimensis* is a medium-sized frog (4–6 cm) with a brown, mottled dorsum and pale belly. It features a distinct dark triangular mark between the eyes and prominent, fleshy toe discs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ombrana sikimensis* is best distinguished by the presence of prominent, elongated, glandular skin folds on its back, which are more distinct than those of similar species.
ai.habitat: *Ombrana sikimensis* inhabits moist, rocky streams within subtropical and temperate broadleaf forests at elevations ranging from 600 to 2,500 meters in the Himalayas.
ai.behavior: The Sikkim Asian Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates along the damp, rocky banks of high-altitude mountain streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ombrana sikimensis* breeds during the monsoon (June–August), laying small clutches of pigmented eggs in slow-flowing mountain streams or rocky pools.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ombrana sikimensis* is found in the Eastern Himalayas, specifically across Sikkim, West Bengal, and Arunachal Pradesh, at elevations between 1,000 and 2,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Sikkim Asian Frog produces a series of short, high-pitched "chirp" notes, typically heard near fast-flowing mountain streams in its rocky, humid habitat.
